risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: Every CSV export on the platform wrote cells as quote + String(c).replace(/quote/g, double) + quote -- correct RFC 4180 quoting and no defence against formula injection. Excel, LibreOffice and Google Sheets execute a cell beginning =, +, - or @ as a formula on open, and the surrounding quotes do not prevent it because the importer strips them as syntax before evaluating. Any user-typed field (customer name, memo, complaint body) was executable content in the recipient spreadsheet, with =cmd reaching DDE and =IMPORTXML exfiltrating the adjacent row. 53 sites across 13 files, one line copied repeatedly; stonedesk.html held 39 of them in 36 script blocks. Four apps were worse than the rest: their quoter was CONDITIONAL and emitted the cell entirely unquoted when it contained no comma, quote or newline, including api/_lib/roofing-gl-export.js whose memo field ships to an accountant for import.

risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: tests/sairndental_ledger_export.js: the arm 'a patient who no longer exists leaves the NAME blank and the ID intact' split the CSV row on commas and indexed by header position, so a preceding cell carrying two adjacent commas was quoted by dntCsvCell(), torn into pieces by the split, and left cells[nameIdx] === '' -- the arm then PASSED with the NAME-IS-ID defect present. That is the same defect the arm had been fixed for two days earlier, one layer down: an assertion satisfied by exactly the thing it is named after. Fixed by asserting cells.length === head.length BEFORE indexing, so a row the naive split cannot line up with its header is a REFUSAL rather than a verdict.

risks.basis: the same app (sairndental) has this defect on record
risks.risk: sairndental.html's addChargeEntry() recorded only procedure_type_id, and a procedure type is a mutable row carrying cdt_code, cdt_version and the effective window. The ADA publishes a new CDT edition annually, so the day a practice updates its catalogue every historical charge silently re-reads the new code and edition -- a charge correctly billed as D1110 under CDT 2025 renders, exports through dnt_charges and reports as whatever the row says today, with no error and no warning. The catalogue had full versioning (cdtStatusFor, cdtMaintenance, effective windows); the transactions had none, so the ledger stopped describing what was actually claimed. cdt_code and cdt_version are now stamped at posting and exported from the charge rather than joined.

risks.basis: the same app (sairndental) has this defect on record
risks.risk: api/_lib/dnt-rollup.js summed money amounts as IEEE754 doubles: `cell.value += n` at the sum branch, and `v += cell.value` again at the totals line. 0.1 + 0.2 reported 0.30000000000000004; one hundred $10.01 charges totalled 1000.9999999999998 -- in a roll-up whose own header promises the totals line agrees with the buckets by construction, serving the SAIRNdental per-location production/collections figures. No crash, no warning; the number was simply not the number the ledger says. Fixed by accumulating integer cents in pass 1 and recovering each bucket's integer losslessly at the totals line, with three regression arms each verified to FAIL on the old code.

risks.basis: the same app (sairndental) has this defect on record
risks.risk: THE CHARGE CDT STAMP WAS WRITTEN AND NEVER READ, AND THE CATALOGUE HAD NO EDIT PATH, so the guarantee the stamping commit stated did not hold and the versioning feature was unreachable for the population it was built for. addChargeEntry() has stamped cdt_code and cdt_version onto every dnt_charges row since 2026-09-17, and its own comment states that the code and edition are STAMPED AT POSTING so a catalogue edit cannot restate history. BOTH readers ignored the stamp and looked the code up live from the mutable procedure-type row: the patient ledger's charges table, and the charges export's Procedure column -- nine lines below its own comment stating the rule it then broke, that a deleted patient still has charges and a name-only export would make those rows unattributable. A deleted or revised procedure type has charges too. The defect is invisible to every structural check because the stamp and the live lookup return the same answer on every row until the day the catalogue is edited, which is the one day the stamp exists for. SECOND HALF: the procedure-type form was ADD-ONLY and the table's only action was Remove, so every row predating the versioning reported 'Not verifiable' permanently with no path to a checked state, and applying a new CDT edition meant Remove-and-re-Add, minting a new row id and orphaning every historical charge -- the exact ledger-integrity failure the stamp was written to prevent, reached by a different door. The stamping fix was therefore written for an edit path that did not exist, which is why its missing read half never surfaced. FIXED: dntChargeCode() is the single reader at both sites, preferring the stamp, falling back to the live row only when there is no stamp and LABELLING that, and saying 'not recorded' when neither exists rather than guessing; three new export columns carry the code and edition as billed and the source of each; and a revise path updates a procedure type in place keeping its row id, appending replaced values to revisions[] rather than overwriting, recording only changed fields, and refusing a no-change, a vanished target and an inverted window. DRIVEN, 22 checks exit 0, first arm being the discriminating case where the catalogue was revised after posting so stamp and lookup disagree. NO TOOL FOUND IT: found by tracing which readers consume a charge's stamped fields after reading addChargeEntry()'s own comment claiming a guarantee; the 22-check driver was written afterwards to prove the fix, not to find the defect.

risks.basis: the same app (sairndental) has this defect on record
risks.risk: rGfe() never compared the stored rec.issued_at to the 149.610(b)(1)(vi) due date, so an estimate issued 46 days past its date rendered identically to one issued on time. REPRODUCED in a browser BEFORE the fix: requested 2026-09-01, due 2026-09-04, marked Issued 2026-10-20, and the Due tile went 1 -> 0 with the nav badge disappearing and the row badge neutral. issueGfe() had stored issued_at since the panel shipped in a002b2dc and NOTHING EVER READ IT, so the whole obligation -- which in (b)(1)(vi) is a DATE -- was dropped while the data to keep it sat on the record. Fixed by rendering three outcomes (issued LATE with the day count, issued in time, issued with timing not on file) plus a late count in the Issued tile sub-line, because fixing only the row would have left the tiles reading clean and the tiles are what gets read.

risks.basis: the same app (sairndental) has this defect on record
risks.risk: rCredentials(null) returned before touching the four KPI tiles, which are hardcoded 0 in the markup, so a panel that had checked nothing showed Expired 0 / Expiring Soon 0 / CE Behind Pace 0 / MATE Outstanding 0 with the nav badge hidden. REPRODUCED in a browser BEFORE the fix with the licence key blanked and two credentials on file expired 21 and 28 months (2025-01-31 and 2024-06-30 against 2026-10-20): all four tiles read 0. Reachable on FOUR silent conditions in sdnEvaluateCredentials() -- no licence key, any non-ok status, an ok status with a non-ok body, any network error -- all four console.warn and return null. Could-not-run is a third state and folding it into passed is PR 1.11 arriving in a KPI tile instead of a gate. Fixed to -- per tile with a tooltip, a ? nav badge, and an empty-table message that says the board could not be evaluated. A NEGATIVE CONTROL was driven because it was needed: a successful board must CLEAR the marks, or a tile that is now a real 0 keeps a tooltip saying it was never checked.

risks.basis: the same app (sairndental) has this defect on record
risks.risk: REPRODUCED with a delayed stubbed fetch before the change: first paint was the could-not-run view with NO_REASON on a first visit, and on a revisit the PREVIOUS attempt's FORBIDDEN "your session is not authorised ... sign in again" while a request that would succeed was in flight. FIXED with a pending state: refreshCredentialBoard(paintPending) counts in-flight evaluations and paints "Checking the credential board" with pending tiles and badge. DRIVEN 37/37: ok/403/500/network each pending-then-outcome, no-licence settles without sticking, overlap holds pending until the last settles, the background refresh leaves a real board up, a throw cannot leave it stuck. MUTATION CONTROL: the pending branch disabled in a routed copy of the page makes the first-paint assertion fail. Severity LOW: transient until the request settles, no data changed -- but the revisit case mis-stated whose problem it was.

risks.basis: the same app (sairndental) has this defect on record

DRIVEN BEFORE AND AFTER, awaiting the real promise rather than sleeping -- four distinct codes with four distinct sentences now: 403 FORBIDDEN "not authorised, this panel is owner-only" (your sign-in), 500 UPSTREAM "the server refused, run its schema first" (the server), NETWORK "could not be reached, check the connection" (the connection), NO_LICENCE "no licence key on this install" (this practice).
